pinout.name: IN
pinout.description: Input supply voltage (1.5 V to 6.0 V operating, 6.5 V abs max); recommend >= 1 uF ceramic decoupling capacitor.

pinout.name: EN
pinout.description: Active-high Smart Enable (VEN(HI) >= 1.1 V, VEN(LOW) <= 0.3 V); 500 kOhm internal pulldown disconnects once enabled.

pinout.name: NC
pinout.description: No internal connection; connect to ground or leave floating.

pinout.name: OUT
pinout.description: Regulated 3.3 V output with 60 Ohm active discharge ('P' suffix); requires 1 uF to 22 uF ceramic cap (>= 0.5 uF effective).

vout_tolerance_pct.condition: ±1.5% over TJ = -40°C to +125°C for VOUT >= 1.5 V (±1% nominal at TJ = 25°C, 1 uA <= IOUT <= 1 mA)

iq_typ_ua.condition: 25 nA (0.025 uA) typ, 46 nA max at IOUT = 0 mA, TJ = 25°C (60 nA max -40..+85°C); stays 25 nA typ even in dropout

design_gotchas.title: Strict 22 uF Maximum Output Capacitance Limit for Loop Stability
design_gotchas.detail: Recommended Operating Conditions (Page 5, Note 2) caps derated output capacitance at 22 uF maximum for loop stability (with 0.5 uF minimum effective capacitance). Do not place large 47 uF–100 uF bulk decoupling capacitors on VOUT as commonly done with conventional LDOs like TLV755P (up to 200 uF).

design_gotchas.title: Slow 1.2 ms Typ (1.6 ms Max) Startup Time & Higher 130 uVRMS Output Noise
design_gotchas.detail: Achieving 25 nA nanopower IQ comes with a 1,200 us typ (1,600 us max) startup time for 3.0 V < VOUT <= 5.0 V (Page 7) and 130 uVRMS noise (vs 7 uVRMS on TPS7A20). Account for the >1.6 ms startup delay in power-sequencing timers and avoid using TPS7A02 for ultra-low-noise RF/ADC analog supplies.

design_gotchas.title: No Internal Reverse-Current Blocking & 5.5 V Absolute Maximum on VOUT
design_gotchas.detail: VOUT absolute maximum is min(VIN + 0.3 V, 5.5 V), and Section 7.3 explicitly warns that reverse current when VIN collapses can damage the device unless limited to <= 5% of rated output current (10 mA) for brief durations or blocked with an external Schottky diode.

design_gotchas.title: Smart Enable 500 kOhm Pulldown Disconnects When Enabled — Ideal for Floating EN
design_gotchas.detail: Unlike standard pull-down LDOs that waste microamps through an EN pulldown resistor while ON, TPS7A02 disconnects its 500 kOhm pulldown once EN > 1.1 V and startup finishes (limiting EN leakage to 10 nA typ), while still safely keeping the regulator OFF if EN floats.

typical_use_cases: Multi-year coin-cell or primary-lithium IoT sensors, smart meters, and smoke detectors needing 25 nA IQ
Always-on wearable MCU standby rails maintaining 25 nA IQ even in battery end-of-life dropout
Battery-powered medical monitors (pulse oximeters, glucose meters) needing 3 nA shelf-life shutdown current
Pin-compatible ultra-low-Iq upgrade for 5-pin SOT-23-5 (1=IN, 2=GND, 3=EN, 4=NC, 5=OUT) boards <= 200 mA
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TPS7A0233PDBVR is a nanopower 200 mA fixed 3.3 V (±1.5% over -40°C to +125°C) LDO in a 5-pin DBV SOT-23-5 package (1=IN, 2=GND, 3=EN active high with smart pulldown, 4=NC, 5=OUT with 60 Ohm active discharge). Operating from 1.5 V to 6.0 V (6.5 V abs max), it achieves a benchmark 25 nA (0.025 uA) quiescent current even in dropout and 3 nA shutdown current, with <= 270 mV max dropout at 200 mA (to 85°C), 55 dB PSRR at 1 kHz, and 181.9 °C/W RθJA. Designers must respect its 22 uF maximum derated output capacitance cap, 1.2–1.6 ms startup time, and lack of reverse-current blocking.
